entry.quote: I think it's a standard behavior, and it's not just Airbnb, but it's generally speaking external booking channels. From the view of a property manager, you try to optimize your yield and fill the rooms you have to fill and the properties you have to fill at the best rate possible and pay the least distribution necessary. Apparently, this means you have an incentive to get as many direct bookings as possible through the big brand awareness and distribution power of the big OTAs, including Airbnb. They yield, there's somewhat of a dependency to also list on them, but in order to see them as an additional distribution channel and not as one of the primary booking channels, normally operators will price up. I'd say probably more than 50% of property managers will price up on Airbnb.
